{"design":"Read on 2026-11-22 against decision mimid-1wgh.97. COMPATIBLE as written; no decision from Mark was needed and no draft change is required to hold mimid's model.

HOW MIMID'S MODEL FITS. mimid-1wgh.97 settled that a did:key may be an alsoKnownAs inside a did:webvh log and never a credential of its own. In this draft's terms that is expressible with no new field: ChatContact.did (server-set, 'the DID's verification methods are the authoritative source of public-key material') carries the did:webvh DID, and the did:key is found by resolving it, since alsoKnownAs is DID Core's. The draft already draws the authority line mimid needs: 'a key not present in the verified did:webvh log carries none of the log's guarantees', and its did:key non-rotatability section says what mimid says — no rotation, a compromised key cannot be recovered, the DID must be retired.

WORK, when picked up:
- Advertise the capability and set ChatContact.did to the user's did:webvh DID where mimid has one.
- Implement did:key resolution, which the draft makes mandatory-to-implement. It is nearly free: deterministic local derivation from the DID URI, no network. It also buys a real check — that an alsoKnownAs did:key entry actually encodes a usable key — which bead mimid-1wgh.4.81.38 can use.
- Never accept a did:key as an MLS credential (mimid-1wgh.97). Resolving a DID and accepting it as a credential are different layers, and conforming to this draft does not require the second.
- The host-less-DID federation verification of this draft belongs with jmap-chat-federation, which mimid is not implementing (mimid-1wgh.101), so it is out of scope here.

DRAFT FEEDBACK FOR MARK, worth raising with himself as author: the draft makes did:key MANDATORY-to-implement and did:webvh only RECOMMENDED. That is the inverse of mimid's priorities and, by the draft's own security considerations, the inverse of the security story: it documents did:key as non-rotatable, unrecoverable on compromise, and 'the floor of self-sovereign identity', while did:webvh is the method that adds a verifiable key history. Mandating the weaker method and merely recommending the stronger one is worth a second look, even if the reason is adoption rather than security."}
